source.title: Some open problems on Feynman periods

accepted.question_text: For the wheel graphs W_n with n ≥ 3, is every convergent generalized Feynman period of W_n a rational linear combination of odd Riemann zeta values only, namely an element of Q + Qζ(3) + ··· + Qζ(2n−3)? Equivalently, must all even zeta values, products of zeta values, and higher-depth multiple zeta values be absent from the period space Pc(W_n)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1. Wheel graphs Wn (n ≥ 3) have only odd Riemann zetas as periods: Pc(Wn) = Q+Qζ (3) +···+Qζ (2n−3). (20)
Notice how far Thm. 3 still is from Eq. (20): We not only have to exclude multiple zeta values, but also all even Riemann zeta values ζ (2k).

accepted.question_text: Does ζ(2) fail to occur as a period of every Feynman graph G? In other words, is it true for all graphs G that the period space Pc(G) does not contain ζ(2)?
accepted.context_brief: Absence of ζ(2) from graph periods

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2. ζ (2) is not a period of any graph: ζ (2) ∈/ Pc(G).
In fact, while ζ (12) is known to appear in periods [39], the even zeta values with lower weight have not been observed as periods of any graph.

accepted.question_text: Is every period of every Feynman graph with at most 5 loops a multiple zeta value? Equivalently, do the graphs with loop number ≤ 5 avoid genuinely non-MZV periods even in the cases where current methods only show that their periods are rational linear combinations of alternating sums or multiple polylogarithms at −1?

evidence.quote: The interesting observation is that all graphs with ≤ 5 loops seem to have only MZV as periods [1, 34, 35]; that is, all periods of the supposedly more complicated graphs (the non-planar ones and the cube) turn out to be MZV.
Conjecture 3. All periods of graphs with ≤ 5 loops are multiple zeta values.

accepted.question_text: Given an arbitrary Feynman graph G, can one decide whether all periods of G belong to the class of multiple polylogarithms, rather than requiring graph-specific sufficient criteria such as vertex-width 3?

evidence.quote: In general it is extremely hard to get a handle on all periods of a Feynman graph, because in most cases it is unknown what kind of numbers to expect.
We will restrict here to very special cases where the periods can be expressed as MPL from Eq. (5). At the moment it is unknown how to decide if an arbitrary given graph belongs to this class.
